module_title: Chemical Bonding: Ionic and Covalent Bonds
introduction: Why don't atoms exist alone? Why do they combine to form molecules? The answer is 'Stability'. Every atom wants to achieve a stable outer shell with 8 electrons (an octet), just like the Noble Gases. To achieve this, atoms form 'Chemical Bonds'.

core_concepts.title: The Octet Rule
core_concepts.description: The tendency of atoms to prefer having eight electrons in their valence shell. Atoms will lose, gain, or share electrons to achieve this stable configuration. (For Hydrogen and Helium, this rule is a 'Duplet' of 2 electrons).

core_concepts.title: Ionic Bond (Electrovalent Bond)
core_concepts.description:
Formed by the 'complete transfer' of one or more electrons from one atom to another. It always forms between a Metal (which loses electrons) and a Non-metal (which gains electrons). 
Example: $NaCl$ (Table Salt). Sodium (Na) donates 1 electron to become a positive ion ($Na^+$), and Chlorine (Cl) accepts it to become a negative ion ($Cl^-$).

core_concepts.title: Covalent Bond
core_concepts.description:
Formed by the 'sharing' of electrons between two atoms. It generally forms between two Non-metals. 
Example: $H_2O$ (Water), $CO_2$, $CH_4$ (Methane). No ions are formed in a pure covalent bond.

core_concepts.title: Properties of Ionic vs. Covalent Compounds
core_concepts.description:
1. Ionic Compounds: Have 'very high' melting and boiling points because the electrostatic force between ions is very strong. They are usually soluble in water. 
2. Covalent Compounds: Have 'low' melting and boiling points. They are generally insoluble in water but soluble in organic solvents (like alcohol or benzene).

important_entities.name: Electrical Conductivity
important_entities.significance: Ionic compounds do NOT conduct electricity in their 'solid state' (because the ions are rigidly locked in a crystal lattice). However, in their 'molten state' or when dissolved in water (aqueous solution), they become excellent conductors because the ions are free to move.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: In a standard covalent bond, both atoms contribute 1 electron to the shared pair. But in a 'Coordinate Covalent Bond' (or Dative Bond), the shared electron pair is donated by ONLY ONE of the participating atoms, though both share it. (Examples: Ozone $O_3$, Ammonium ion $NH_4^+$).

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Ionic = I Own it (Donation/Transfer). Covalent = Co-operate (Sharing).
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Metals are generous donors (Ionic). Non-metals are business partners who share (Covalent).

exam_strategy_tips: A direct question in SSC exams: 'Which type of bond is present in a molecule of Sodium Chloride ($NaCl$)?' Answer: Ionic Bond (or Electrovalent Bond).
